# BladeMaster and DexLab: Introduction to Soft Body Cutting Simulation

Cut a piece of tofu-like soft body, then remove the knife and push aside the cut portion. It seems simple, but it requires the simulation tool to handle material deformation, topological separation, and surface contact simultaneously. This chapter starts from the cutting mechanism of BladeMaster, and introduces the open-source CPU implementation of DexLab, as well as the banana and tofu experiment interfaces.

## 1. What is seen in the video

[ REDnote demonstration ](https://www.xiaohongshu.com/explore/6ad0dd96000000001c02fb40) shows the tool cutting banana and tofu-like materials. [ DexLab banana experiment page ](https://huangkiki.github.io/Dexlab/zh-cn/latest/banana-cutting.html) provides surface and particle views, dividing the material into four sections with three continuous cuts; [ tofu experiment page ](https://huangkiki.github.io/Dexlab/zh-cn/latest/cutting.html) demonstrates cutting, removing the tool, and using unilateral diagnostic impulse tests to verify whether the cut material can move independently. Colors are used to distinguish the cutting history, and determining separation also requires considering connection relationships and motion records.

The geometric and material parameters of bananas are synthetic settings and have not been calibrated for real bananas yet; this experiment does not include a robotic arm or learning policy. The Xiaohongshu author referenced TLMPM and persistent cutting history from the paper in their implementation, which is a independently written CPU-optimized solution. The original paper, BladeMaster, uses GPU acceleration, and the performance and scope of implementation between the two cannot be directly compared.

## 2. Why Memory is Needed for Cutouts

If the transfer between traditional particles and grids crosses a cutting edge, the materials on both sides may be coupled numerically again after the blade is removed. BladeMaster uses the Total Lagrangian Material Point Method (TLMPM), which records persistent side labels for material points based on the geometry of the cutting edge. These labels control the coupling between particles and grids: materials that remain connected retain the transfer, while no reconnection occurs on both sides of the cutting edge. Contact treatment is also required between the cutting edges to enable them to contact and slide again; the bidirectional coupling between the blade and material allows the material's reaction force to affect the movement of the blade.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[刀具轨迹与材料粒子] --> B[更新切割侧别与历史]
    B --> C[按相容关系传递粒子与网格动量]
    C --> D[材料接触与刀具反力]
    D --> E[保存状态并检查切后运动]
```

The original paper supports progressive and cross-cutting methods; the support scope for specific reproduction projects should be based on their corresponding version experiment pages. The豆腐 baseline in DexLab uses limited straight knives and persistent labels, combined with dynamic tools, contact force, and independent scorers; its reconstructed surface shows an approximation.

## 3. Reading and running experiments

First, open [DexLab repository ](https://github.com/huangkiki/Dexlab) and its [ banana case description ](https://github.com/huangkiki/Dexlab/tree/main/demos/banana-cut). Observe the segmented sections after three cuts in the particle view. The [ full experiment page ](https://huangkiki.github.io/Dexlab/zh-cn/latest/cutting.html) for the tofu case provides information on environmental dependencies, resource limits, execution commands, and acceptance thresholds. Before running, configure the DexLab environment, shared lock, and data directory according to this page; the output directory should be a new directory.

The experiment will save the physical state, trajectory, and scoring results. To determine whether cutting is completed, check `score.json` and the scorer exit code, rather than only relying on whether the animation or runner exits successfully. The tofu baseline also provides cases of partial cutting, uncut, and time-step sensitivity; they help distinguish between real material separation and visual cuts. The results on time-step sensitivity in the project report show significant changes in the peak反力, and convergence of cutting force has not been established yet. Therefore, these results are suitable for learning mechanisms and numerical checks, but cannot be directly used as a force calibration for real materials.

## 4. Further Reading

- [BladeMaster project page ](https://jango6324.github.io/blademaster/) and [ papers ](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.27342): original methods, cutting, and manipulation demonstrations.
- [DexLab tofu experiment ](https://huangkiki.github.io/Dexlab/zh-cn/latest/cutting.html): CPU implementation, parameters, controls, and reproduction commands.
- [DexLab banana experiment ](https://huangkiki.github.io/Dexlab/zh-cn/latest/banana-cutting.html): three consecutive cuts and switchable surface, particle replay.
